chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, concerning:
A woman who committed zina while she was insane—he said: “She does not possess control of her affair, and there is no rajm upon her nor banishment.”

And he said regarding a woman who confessed about herself that a man had compelled her against herself: “She is like one overpowered, not possessing herself; if he wished, he could have killed her. There is no flogging upon her, nor banishment, nor rajm.”

key_terms.لَا تَمْلِكُ أَمْرَهَا: she does not control her own affair; indicating absence of responsible agency
key_terms.مَجْنُونَةٌ: insane; lacking legal capacity and accountability
key_terms.نَفْيٌ: banishment or exile as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment for zina applied to an insane or coerced woman in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the hadd punishment for zina is not applied to a woman who lacked legal agency, such as one who was insane or one who was coerced. It emphasizes the juristic principle that criminal liability depends on possession of one's will and control over one's actions.
